title: No work under the Germans; the American consul says stay hidden
summary: Briggs stopped playing, as French musicians were hostile, and the American consul Murphy told Americans to stay undercover.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And you hadn't continued to work as a musician?

That stopped, immediately. I had many propositions to work, but I did not work, because I knew that I would not be permitted to work. And the attitude of the French musicians didn't encourage me to try to work.
The attitude of the French musician was entirely hostile to
knowing the German mentality, with certain people, they had just taken advantage of it, you see.

I had propositions -- that is when the Germans came in I was at the Club Pierre Charon on the Champs Elysee, and the proprietor sent for us to come back after the Germans left. And when I went down to the Consulate, the Consul told me that it would be best to stay undercover.
He told us all, those who stayed, 'cause there were quite a few that stayed, to stay undercover. We explained that we had work and everything. He thought, Mr. Murphy --
The American Consul. His name was Mr. Murphy, a rather well known diplomat. He advised us to stay undercover, 'cause he was right.
He said, "Do you have enough money

to live?" We said, "Yes, we do." And he said, "Well, stay undercover," he said, "Go in the streets only when you have to." And that's what I did until Japan -- But before then, something had happened. I showed you a picture yesterday of Aime Barelli.
